newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria central bank sees room for rate cuts.
newsitem.headline: Austria central bank sees room for rate cuts.

text.p: The Austrian central bank said on Thursday short-term rates could have further room to fall.
"Looking at inflation and other economic developments, I see room for an interest rate cut in the securities repurchase rate and the Gomex money market rate," Liebscher said.
Liebscher, speaking at an investment fair in Vienna, declined to specify a timeframe for possible rate reductions.
Austria's repo rate stands at three percent, while the Gomex rate is at 3.4 percent. The discount rate is at 2.5 percent, and the Lombard at 4.75 percent.
The central bank chief said he saw no reason to expect a cut in the discount rate, but added any change in key rates would be made in lockstep with other European central banks.

Annual inflation edged down to 1.8 percent in August from 1.9 percent in July. Analysts widely expect the Austrian economy to grow by less than one percent this year, down from 1.8 percent last year. -- Vienna newsroom +431 53112 274
